title: Dose Chain Log
user: A person taking several medicines at common times or with an after-taken interval who needs to confirm a group quickly and schedule follow-ups from the actual taken time.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A 2026 launch for an open-source Android medication reminder shows continuing demand for a privacy-respecting alternative in this sensitive category.
A MedTimer user taking around ten medicines says individual confirmation is annoying and requests grouped taken/skipped/reschedule actions.

recurrence: Medication-reminder tools continue to launch, while users with multiple medicines identify batch confirmation as a repeated, accessibility-relevant friction point.
current_workaround: Tap many individual reminders, set separate phone alarms, or use a general medication app that treats every dose as an independent event.
incumbents_and_gap: Medisafe, MyTherapy, Apple Health Medications, and MedTimer provide reminders. A constrained local event log centered on group confirmation and actual-time follow-up chains is a smaller unmet workflow.
smallest_useful_product: Android app with user-configured medicine labels, grouped time windows, taken/skipped/late event logging, and optional follow-up timers anchored to a recorded taken time.
constraints: Sensitive health data remains on device and is exportable only by the user; notification reliability must follow Android requirements; include clear non-medical-advice and emergency guidance boundaries.
success_measure: In a 30-day opt-in pilot, users with three or more concurrent medicines record 85% of configured group events and need fewer than two taps per group confirmation on median.
why_distinct: It handles the temporal relationship among already prescribed doses, not diagnosis, prescription, or generic reminder gamification.
